./deploy.sh YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME

github.com/new → name it edemscot-forex → uploading an existing file → drag the folder contents → Settings → Pages → main / (root).

Why asking twice was my fault, not yours. The CSS was correct when you asked the second time, but you couldn't see it. The saved state in your browser loads on top of the shipped defaults:

JavaScript
merged.messages = Array.isArray(db.messages) ? db.messages : base.messages;

That line keeps whatever messages are already stored — correct behaviour, since a returning user's own messages must never be thrown away. But it meant that when I added the outgoing replies to the sample thread, any browser that had already loaded the app once kept the old incoming-only thread permanently. My tests used fresh profiles, so they passed while your page stayed old. That's the gap.

The fix: a one-time migration that reads the version from the saved object and appends the three replies to the sample thread only if it's untouched. It briefly failed too — Object.assign({}, base, db) copies msgSeedVersion:2 out of the defaults before the check runs, so every old save looked current and the migration never fired. Reading db.msgSeedVersion from the stored object fixed it.

I audited all 93 pages at 390px and desktop. Three real appearance defects found and fixed.

What was broken

1. Tab labels cut mid-word — 5 workspaces
The Rail in Freelancing, Digital Store, Social, Advertising and Wallet scrolled sideways with the scrollbar hidden. On a phone you saw Browse Cat, Social Media Grow, Request a UGC video — a label sliced through its own letters. That reads as a broken render, not "swipe for more." I first added a fade cue, but the dimmed edge fell on the tab you were aiming at and the word was still cut, so I made the strips wrap instead. Every destination is now fully readable at every width.

2. Service descriptions sliced through the letters
.fl-clamp used -webkit-line-clamp:3. In this engine display:-webkit-box silently resolves to flow-root, so the clamp never applied — the third line was simply chopped mid-letter with no ellipsis to signal anything was missing. Since cutting a seller's own words is the same information loss as truncating a filename, the full description now shows.

3. My own fix broke accessibility, and I caught it
Wrapping with min-height:32px dropped 18 controls below your 44×44 rule — a11y went to 13/1. The rail can grow taller; the hit area cannot shrink. Restored to 44px, back to 14/0.
